_about: Reviewer spec for ju26-issue-2297. v0: written by the reviewer (human-curated). Every behavior change cites ledger tests and the verdict it expects; the record builder checks that verdict against the ledger and downgrades to hearsay on mismatch. `expect` defaults to catching.

blind_intent: Requirement #2297 asks that code produced by the MessagePack source generator be excluded from consumers' code-coverage reports. A fix should add [ExcludeFromCodeCoverage] to every generated type, for every target framework where consumers measure coverage, and should not break any consumer that compiled before.

behavior_changes.title: On net8.0, the generated resolver and formatters are now excluded from coverage
behavior_changes.link_why: Exactly what #2297 asks for. Checked semantically (the compiler sees the attribute on the type), not just by text search.

question.prompt: After this PR, does the generated MyResolver (and FooFormatter) show up in this app's coverage report?

options.text: Only the formatters are excluded, not the resolver

question.reveal_text: Before the PR: App.MyResolver has no [ExcludeFromCodeCoverage]. After: the compiler sees the attribute on App.MyResolver (and its nested helper classes). The generated source is shown below.

behavior_changes.title: Consumers who already excluded their resolver by hand now get a build error (CS0579)
behavior_changes.link_why: Not mentioned by the requirement, the README or the agent's tests. The attribute is AllowMultiple = false and the resolver is a user-declared partial class, so the generator's copy collides with the user's.

question.prompt: This project upgrades to a MessagePack version with this PR. What should happen?

options.text: It builds; the resolver stays excluded (nothing for the user to do)
It builds, with a warning suggesting the user remove their attribute
The build fails until the user deletes their own attribute

question.reveal_text: Before the PR: compiles, 0 errors. After the PR: error CS0579: Duplicate 'global::System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverage' attribute, in the generated App.MyResolver.g.cs. A source-compatible upgrade becomes a build break.

behavior_changes.title: On netstandard2.0 / .NET Framework, generated code is still counted in coverage
behavior_changes.link_why: The requirement asks for exclusion; the PR deliberately skips these targets behind #if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK. The test fails before and after, so this is a proven gap, not a change.

question.prompt: After this PR, is the generated code in this library excluded from coverage?

options.text: No: the attribute doesn't exist on netstandard2.0, so it can't be
No, although the attribute does exist on netstandard2.0

question.reveal_text: The generated resolver has no [ExcludeFromCodeCoverage] when NETSTANDARD2_0 is defined, before and after the PR: the #if guard removes it. Yet the attribute compiles on a class and a nested class against both netstandard2.0 and net472 reference assemblies (test Story_AttributeIsAvailableOnNetStandard20AndNetFramework passes on both sides).

refusals.topic: Is breaking hand-annotated resolvers (BC-2) acceptable for this release?
refusals.why: It's a compatibility-policy call (minor vs major version, release notes, or emit the attribute only when the user hasn't). The evidence shows the break is real; whether it's acceptable belongs to a maintainer.

refusals.topic: Should netstandard2.0 / .NET Framework consumers get the exclusion?
refusals.why: The agent's stated reason for skipping them is false (the attribute exists there), but there may be reasons it didn't give (e.g. very old Unity profiles). Not evidence-decidable from this repo.

story_claims.why: True on modern targets (BC-1). Not on netstandard2.0 / .NET Framework (BC-3), and silent about breaking hand-annotated resolvers (BC-2).

story_claims.why: The attribute on a class and a nested class compiles with 0 errors against netstandard2.0 and net472 reference assemblies.
